headline: Royal Australian Air Force Recruitment in 2026
metaDescription: Join the Royal Australian Air Force in 2026: roles, age and education requirements, the ADF Careers application process, fitness tests and recruit training.

sections.content:
The Royal Australian Air Force, or RAAF, offers general entry, trade and officer roles across flying, engineering, logistics, intelligence, cyber, communications, medical and support fields. Pilots and aircrew fly and operate aircraft, while engineers and technicians keep them airworthy. Logistics, administration and catering roles keep bases running day to day.

General entry roles are open to people with no prior experience, and most require completion of Year 10 with passes in English and mathematics, with science or physics needed for some technical specialisations. Officer roles involve leading teams and managing complex operations, and can be entered with or without a university degree.
sections.title: Roles in the Royal Australian Air Force

sections.content:
You must be at least 17 years old on the day you join the RAAF, although you can start your application from 16 years and 6 months. Applicants under 18 need written approval from both parents or legal guardians. For entry to the Australian Defence Force Academy, you can start applying from 16.

You must be an Australian citizen to serve, although permanent residents may be eligible for some roles. You also need a checkable background for the past ten years for security clearance purposes. The minimum education level is generally Year 10 English and mathematics, while officer and pilot roles usually require Year 12 passes in English, mathematics and other subjects.
sections.title: Who can apply: age, citizenship and education

sections.content:
Applications are made through ADF Careers, the Australian Defence Force's official recruiting service, which recruits all year round across Australia. The process starts with an online application and an aptitude test, followed by medical assessments, a fitness test and selection interviews.

For pilot candidates there is an additional aviation screening program. Shortlisted candidates then receive an offer and an enlistment date. The process can take several months, so applicants are advised to start early and to prepare for the fitness and aptitude stages while their application is being assessed.
sections.title: The application process through ADF Careers

sections.content:
Successful general entry recruits begin with a 13-week recruit course at RAAF Base Wagga in New South Wales, which covers military skills, fitness, discipline and teamwork. After that, recruits move into specialist employment training for their chosen role, which can last from a few months to over a year depending on the trade.

Officer cadets complete a 17-week Initial Officer Course at RAAF Base East Sale in Victoria, followed by specialist training. Another pathway is the Australian Defence Force Academy in Canberra, where officer cadets are paid to study for a university degree while training as officers. The RAAF also offers a Gap Year program and work experience for those still deciding.
